tests.what: GET /api/products?q= with all-lowercase query returns products whose names use different casing
GET /api/products?q= with all-uppercase query returns products whose names are lowercase/mixed-case
GET /api/products?q= with mixed-case partial substring matches product names regardless of casing
Typing a query with casing different from the product name into search-input filters the visible product-card list case-insensitively

plan.reason: Case-insensitive matching is a core user-facing search behavior explicitly specified in the contract and a likely spot for a seeded casing bug (e.g., case-sensitive comparison).

proposal.evidence: Line 15 diff: GET /api/products?q=laptop returned 200 with items [] instead of ['Aurora Laptop'] — the lowercase query matched nothing, so the server-side search is case-sensitive, violating REQ-CAT-03; the UI assertions were never reached and the earlier product-card count of 6 passed, so the data exists and the API filtering is at fault

evidence: Deterministic failure: 3/3 attempts failed on clean code, so this is not flaky behavior.

The lowercase-query request returned HTTP 200 (assertion on line 13 passed), but body.items was Array [] instead of ['Aurora Laptop'] — the API filtered out a product that should match, consistent with case-sensitive search logic violating REQ-CAT-03.

The failure appears both on clean code and with the bug enabled with the same signature, so it is not attributable to an injected bug, and the 200-with-empty-result pattern rules out environment/infra errors (no 4xx/5xx, timeout, or connection failure).
missing: Response to a case-exact control query (e.g., q=Aurora Laptop) from the trace.zip proving the product exists in seed data — this would definitively rule out a test-bug (wrong query string or missing fixture product).
